doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Life in the band, the Vegas career path, and 14 trumpet players
summary: Roommates Corky Corcoran and Sonny Payne, how sidemen used the band to reach Vegas, and Bobby Shew's remark that Radke outlasted a revolving chair.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Corcoran and I have become very close, roommates, and then when Corky’s wife was with them I roomed with Sonny. So Sonny and I were really close. And so it was like Red Carey, Perciful, the great pianist that was with him for years, Sonny, Corky, myself, and it was kind of, I was in that kind of a different clique than the younger guys.
Were some of the chairs the second tenor and third trombone etcetera filled by local guys that when the band moved on maybe they didn’t go with the band?

No. No. See in those days everybody went to high schools, went to a hot shot college, went to a jazz camp, got their degree finally from college, then they got on a band, and they got on a band to get to Vegas, when they got on Vegas then they’d jump off in Vegas. And then you’d stay in Vegas. If you were really good in Vegas, like Tommy and those guys, then you were invited to L.A. That was the plan.

That was the path. And Harry used to get bugged because guys would get on the band and then would jump band in Vegas. But I didn’t want to do that you know. And I just — and Harry, I think that he went through something like 14 first trumpet players in like two months before I got there. In fact Bobby Shew was in Vegas and he came to pick me up and we knew each other, you know, from the NORAD days. I remember him picking me up. He probably doesn’t even remember this but he says, “You know everybody’s talking about you, you’re the only guy that’s been with Harry for more than two months in that chair.”
